title: Idaho AI Laws

reading.body:
Idaho's three AI laws regulate uses of AI, not the compute or power behind it. The state has legislated on conversational AI safety, synthetic media, and classroom use, and has said nothing about data centers, electricity, or model training.

The pattern is consumer and institutional protection. S1297 targets operators of public conversational AI, requiring disclosure that a user may be talking to a machine, a suicide-response protocol, and limits aimed at minors. H0727 criminalizes disclosing explicit synthetic media and revises video voyeurism law. S1227 puts the State Department of Education at the center of K-12 generative AI policy, with district-level rules, literacy standards, and vendor disclosure.

For AI specifically, these laws attach obligations to the point of use rather than the point of production. They do not touch siting, interconnection, or load, so they neither accelerate nor constrain the physical buildout that the rest of this site tracks. A reader looking for Idaho's position on the grid as an AI constraint will not find it here.

What the data does not cover is equally clear. It records three enacted laws with passage dates in March 2026 and an effective date of July 1, 2026 for H0727, but it does not give the effective dates of S1297 or S1227, the size of any penalty, appropriations, or whether further bills are pending. It is a snapshot of enacted text, not a measure of enforcement or impact.

body_html:
Idaho has enacted 3 AI-related laws. Each is read from its enrolled text: what it does, who it applies to, when it takes effect, and what it requires.

Enacted AI laws in Idaho

3 laws this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • S1297: Adds to existing law to establish the Conversational AI Safety Act. passed 2026-03-31

    The Conversational AI Safety Act requires operators of conversational AI services accessible to the general public to disclose when users may be misled into thinking they are interacting with a human, to adopt a protocol for responding to suicidal ideation, and to avoid claiming to provide professional mental health care. It imposes additional requirements for minor account holders, including disclosures, limits on engagement rewards, and measures to prevent sexual content and human impersonation. It provides for enforcement by the attorney general through injunctions and civil penalties.

  • H0727: Amends existing law to revise a provision regarding video voyeurism and to revise a penalty for disclosing explicit synthetic media. passed 2026-03-25

    Amends Idaho Code Section 18-6605 to revise video voyeurism definitions and prohibitions. Adds Section 18-6606 to criminalize disclosing explicit synthetic media, with misdemeanor and felony penalties. Declares an emergency and sets an effective date of July 1, 2026.

  • S1227: Adds to existing law to establish provisions regarding generative artificial intelligence in public education. passed 2026-03-19

    This chapter requires the Idaho State Department of Education to develop a statewide generative artificial intelligence in education framework, subject to State Board of Education approval, for K 12 public schools. It requires local school districts and public charter schools to adopt policies governing generative AI use by students and employees, and it directs the State Department of Education to develop literacy standards, assessment guidelines, professional development, and a parental guidance document. It also imposes procurement and vendor disclosure requirements for generative AI tools and grants the State Board of Education rulemaking authority.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Idaho. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
